title: What is OTA? Update options for Arduino and ESP32

spans.text: OTA (Over-The-Air) updates a device over a network instead of plugging in a USB cable. For example, new firmware can be sent over Wi-Fi to a greenhouse sensor. OTA makes remote maintenance easier, but the device needs a safe recovery path if power or connectivity fails.

The key difference is how firmware reaches the board: USB/serial needs a computer and cable nearby; OTA transfers it over Wi-Fi or another network. ArduinoOTA makes IDE uploads convenient for supported Wi-Fi boards such as ESP32/ESP8266. A web updater uses a browser on the local network. An HTTPS pull update downloads a file from a server. ESP-IDF OTA can use two app slots (A/B), write to the inactive slot, and return to the previous image if the new one fails its first boot checks.

Not every board supports OTA: a classic UNO has no Wi-Fi and cannot update itself over a network without extra hardware and a suitable design. Do not confuse an ordinary USB upload with OTA. Check the board, flash layout, bootloader, and official core support first.

spans.code:
build firmware
check board + version
transfer over a supported link
verify image
install, reboot, run health checks
keep old image until confirmed

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Test updates on your own board first. Do not install an unsigned or unvalidated image; plan recovery for power loss.
